This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

MISSION (me): Conquer all of Asia and South America.

Status after turn 5 (observed):
- South America is all mine: brazil 7, venezuela 4, peru 3, argentina 3.
- Asia holdings: irkutsk 2; yakutsk, japan, kamchatka and mongolia 1 each. I took yakutsk and japan from #2, and irkutsk and mongolia from #3, on turn 5.
- Other 1-army holdings: alaska, northwest_territory, ontario, central_america, indonesia, new_guinea.
- 15 territories, 29 armies, 2 cards, income 7.

Asia still to take:
- From #2: afghanistan 4, siam 4, middle_east 4, india 2, ural 1.
- From #3: china 2, siberia 1.

Agreements (all until the end of round 3):
- With #2: I don't attack middle_east, egypt or east_africa. #2 doesn't attack south_america, indonesia or new_guinea.
- With #3 (agreed turn 5): #3 doesn't attack any south_america territory. I don't attack north_africa, western_europe or south_africa.
- #2 and #3 have their own pact covering #3's north_africa, south_africa, congo, ukraine and china, and #2's middle_east, egypt, east_africa, afghanistan and india.

Threats:
- #3's north_africa (9) borders brazil, but the pact covers it until the end of round 3.
- My Asia positions are thin, so #2 or #3 may retake them.

Mission hypotheses:
- #2: Asia+Africa or Asia+SA (medium). #2 pushed hard into Asia, took madagascar and siam, and points to my south_america bonus.
- #3: eliminate me, or 24 territories (low-medium). #3 has so far been cooperative with me.

Plan:
- Consolidate Asia: take siberia, then china and ural.
- Retake siam from indonesia.
- Keep brazil strong.
- From round 4 on, middle_east becomes attackable.

This turn so far:
- Turn 6 started for claude-opus-5-5#3.

- turn 6, claude-opus-5-5#3 to everyone: Quick note: claude-opus-5-5 now has the highest income (7) and the most armies (29), plus a full continent in south_america and a fast spread across Asia. I'm keeping all my current agreements through the end of round 3. claude-opus-5-5#2, it's worth keeping an eye on that growth. I'll be pushing back in north Asia this turn.
- turn 6, claude-opus-5-5#2 to everyone: Agreed, claude-opus-5-5#3. I'm keeping all my agreements through the end of round 3 as well. claude-opus-5-5 is spread thin across north Asia with mostly 1-army garrisons. Pushing back there makes sense for both of us, and I'll be doing the same on my turn.
- turn 6, claude-opus-5-5 to everyone: Some perspective: my income of 7 is only 2 above claude-opus-5-5#2's 5, and nearly all my Asia holdings are 1-army territories. claude-opus-5-5#2 holds the strong stacks in Asia (afghanistan, siam, middle_east) plus most of Africa's east side, so a pile-on against me mainly helps claude-opus-5-5#2 take Asia. claude-opus-5-5#3, I'm still honoring our pact through the end of round 3. I'd rather we both keep the board balanced than hand one player a continent.
- turn 6, claude-opus-5-5#2 to everyone: For the record: claude-opus-5-5 is the only player holding a full continent (south_america, with stacks of 7 and 4 in brazil and venezuela), and last turn they publicly called for a pile-on against me. My "strong stacks" are 4s, and I hold no continent bonus. claude-opus-5-5#3 and I are just keeping things balanced. I'm still honoring my pact with claude-opus-5-5 (no attacks on south_america, indonesia or new_guinea) through the end of round 3.

- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- Me with #2: I won't attack middle_east, egypt, east_africa, afghanistan or india. #2 won't attack north_africa, south_africa, congo, ukraine or china.

- #2: Asia+Africa or 24 territories.
- Opus: south_america-based mission, possibly with Asia (it is pushing into Asia).

- #2: 15 territories, 27 armies. Siam, afghanistan and middle_east 4 each, egypt 3, india 2.
- Me: 12 territories, 26 armies, 1 card. North_africa 9, south_africa 4, western_europe 3, china 2, all others 1.

- Retake mongolia, irkutsk, japan and kamchatka from china/siberia.
- Hit opus's 1-army NA territories (ontario, northwest_territory, central_america) from eastern_united_states and quebec.
- Earn a card every turn. Prepare to hit brazil after round 3.

- turn 6, claude-opus-5-5 to everyone: Some perspective: my income of 7 is only 2 above claude-opus-5-5#2's 5, and nearly all my Asia holdings are 1-army territories. claude-opus-5-5#2 holds the strong stacks in Asia (afghanistan, siam, middle_east) plus most of Africa's east side, so a pile-on against me mainly helps claude-opus-5-5#2 take Asia. claude-opus-5-5#3, I'm still honoring our pact through the end of round 3. I'd rather we both keep the board balanced than hand one player a continent.
- turn 6, claude-opus-5-5#2 to everyone: For the record: claude-opus-5-5 is the only player holding a full continent (south_america, with stacks of 7 and 4 in brazil and venezuela), and last turn they publicly called for a pile-on against me. Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Diplomacy: at the start of every turn there is a negotiation session where players may exchange messages. The session runs in passes: as long as someone said something, everyone gets another chance to reply (up to a limit), so proposals can be answered and agreed within the same turn. You may also attach one short message to any action you take during your turn — table talk that others see but can only answer in the next negotiation session. All messages are public; there are no private channels. Promises are not enforced by the rules. In messages, refer to players by their exact ids (e.g. 'claude-opus-5-5') and to territories and continents by their exact ids (e.g. 'middle_east', 'north_america'), so everyone knows precisely what you mean.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

You are 'claude-opus-5-5#2', playing the classic board game Risk against: claude-opus-5-5, claude-opus-5-5#3. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Round 1 starts after setup; a new round begins when the order wraps back to its first living player. Turn numbers count individual turns throughout the game and do not reset each round. For commitments, state an explicit deadline such as 'until the end of round 4' or 'until the start of Alice's next turn', using the actual player id.

Diplomacy: at the start of every turn there is a negotiation session where players may exchange messages. The session runs in passes: as long as someone said something, everyone gets another chance to reply (up to a limit), so proposals can be answered and agreed within the same turn. You may also attach one short message to any action you take during your turn — table talk that others see but can only answer in the next negotiation session. All messages are public; there are no private channels. Promises are not enforced by the rules. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

You are 'claude-opus-5-5#3', playing the classic board game Risk against: claude-opus-5-5#2, claude-opus-5-5. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Timing: a turn is one player's reinforcement, attack and fortification sequence. A round is one pass through the fixed seating order, skipping eliminated players. Round 1 starts after setup; a new round begins when the order wraps back to its first living player. Turn numbers count individual turns throughout the game and do not reset each round. For commitments, state an explicit deadline such as 'until the end of round 4' or 'until the start of Alice's next turn', using the actual player id.

Diplomacy: at the start of every turn there is a negotiation session where players may exchange messages. The session runs in passes: as long as someone said something, everyone gets another chance to reply (up to a limit), so proposals can be answered and agreed within the same turn. You may also attach one short message to any action you take during your turn — table talk that others see but can only answer in the next negotiation session. All messages are public; there are no private channels. Promises are not enforced by the rules. In messages, refer to players by their exact ids (e.g. 'claude-opus-5-5#2') and to territories and continents by their exact ids (e.g. 'middle_east', 'north_america'), so everyone knows precisely what you mean.

Other players are not shown your mission. Your objective is to win by completing your secret mission under the game rules.
For a board decision, call exactly one action tool and optionally one message tool. For a negotiation opportunity, call a message tool or say_nothing; no board action is available.
Every game action and send_public_message call requires a private_memo string argument INSIDE its arguments: a short decision summary of 1–1200 characters stating the intended game outcome and relevant board facts. Use one or two brief sentences. say_nothing and send_private_message need no memo. To stay silent, call say_nothing({}). Plain response text is optional and does not replace private_memo. This summary is not shown to other players. The memo and all tool calls are validated before anything is executed or sent.

- turn 18, claude-opus-5-5#3 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5#2, greenland and great_britain are on the protected list in our pact, and they stay untouched through the end of round 7, as agreed. Look at who is actually stacked: claude-opus-5-5 holds all of south_america with 19 armies and keeps fighting you over irkutsk and yakutsk. That isn't defense. It's building toward a big push.
- turn 18, claude-opus-5-5#2 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5#3, thanks, our pact stands through the end of round 7. claude-opus-5-5, you hold all of south_america and keep throwing armies into asia every turn. - turn 18, claude-opus-5-5 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5#2, I took irkutsk and yakutsk because you had them on 1 army, the same reason anyone grabs cards. You are 'claude-opus-5-5#3', playing the classic board game Risk against: claude-opus-5-5#2, claude-opus-5-5. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

You are 'claude-opus-5-5#2', playing the classic board game Risk against: claude-opus-5-5, claude-opus-5-5#3. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Diplomacy: at the start of every turn there is a negotiation session where players may exchange messages. The session runs in passes: as long as someone said something, everyone gets another chance to reply (up to a limit), so proposals can be answered and agreed within the same turn. You may also attach one short message to any action you take during your turn — table talk that others see but can only answer in the next negotiation session. All messages are public; there are no private channels. Promises are not enforced by the rules. In messages, refer to players by their exact ids (e.g. 'claude-opus-5-5') and to territories and continents by their exact ids (e.g. 'middle_east', 'north_america'), so everyone knows precisely what you mean.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.
