This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.

- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.

Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.

- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.

- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.

Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

You are 'claude-opus-5-5#2', playing the classic board game Risk against: claude-opus-5-5, claude-opus-5-5#3. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

You are 'claude-opus-5-5', playing the classic board game Risk against: claude-opus-5-5#2, claude-opus-5-5#3. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

You are 'claude-opus-5-5#3', playing the classic board game Risk against: claude-opus-5-5#2, claude-opus-5-5. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Timing: a turn is one player's reinforcement, attack and fortification sequence. A round is one pass through the fixed seating order, skipping eliminated players. Round 1 starts after setup; a new round begins when the order wraps back to its first living player. Turn numbers count individual turns throughout the game and do not reset each round. For commitments, state an explicit deadline such as 'until the end of round 4' or 'until the start of Alice's next turn', using the actual player id.

Diplomacy: at the start of every turn there is a negotiation session where players may exchange messages. The session runs in passes: as long as someone said something, everyone gets another chance to reply (up to a limit), so proposals can be answered and agreed within the same turn. You may also attach one short message to any action you take during your turn — table talk that others see but can only answer in the next negotiation session. All messages are public; there are no private channels. Promises are not enforced by the rules. In messages, refer to players by their exact ids (e.g. 'claude-opus-5-5') and to territories and continents by their exact ids (e.g. 'middle_east', 'north_america'), so everyone knows precisely what you mean.

Use one or two brief sentences. say_nothing and send_private_message need no memo. To stay silent, call say_nothing({}). Plain response text is optional and does not replace private_memo. This summary is not shown to other players. The memo and all tool calls are validated before anything is executed or sent.

attack phase. It is your move.

- Oceania is all mine: indonesia 4, the rest 1.
- Asia, I hold 7: china 3, japan 2, irkutsk/siberia/yakutsk/kamchatka/mongolia 1 each.

**Missing for my mission (5 territories):**
- opus holds india 1 and siam 3.
- #3 holds middle_east 1, afghanistan 1 and ural 1.

**Turn 42:** #3 took southern_europe, ural, middle_east and afghanistan from opus. #3 now has 19 territories, all at 1 army, 4 cards, income 16 (north_america + europe).

**opus:** 6 territories, 10 armies, 5 cards (must trade), income 5. Holds south_america plus india and siam.

**Pact with #3:** no attacks on each other through the end of round 15, which is turns 43-45. My turn 43 falls inside it, so I can't attack middle_east, afghanistan or ural this turn without breaking my word.
- I confirmed I won't attack western_europe, ukraine or alaska.
- #3 confirmed it won't attack north_africa or kamchatka.

**Hypotheses:**
- opus: asia + south_america (medium-high).
- #3: possibly 24 territories or a europe/north_america combo (it's at 19). It is now the main threat.

**Plan:**
- This turn: take india and siam from opus. Reinforce china, egypt and east_africa.
- Round 16: hit #3's thin asia holdings.
- Push the argument that #3 is now the leader.

- turn 43, claude-opus-5-5#2 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5, thanks for the offer, but I can't sign a full non-aggression pact. india and siam sit inside my area and I don't want to promise something I might not keep. What I can say plainly: from round 16 on, my armies will be pointed at claude-opus-5-5#3's thin positions. claude-opus-5-5#3, take a look at your own numbers. You have 19 territories and 16 armies a turn, and 24 territories is one card trade away for you. Asking everyone to keep fighting me while you collect the biggest income on the board just protects the leader.
- turn 43, claude-opus-5-5 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5#3 is 5 territories away from 24 and gets 16 armies a turn. That makes it the immediate threat, whatever its mission card says. claude-opus-5-5#2, fair enough on the pact. All I ask is that you leave india and siam alone this turn. On my turn I'll take back afghanistan, ural and middle_east from claude-opus-5-5#3, which cuts its territory count, and from round 16 we can both keep pressure on its 1-army lines.
- turn 43, claude-opus-5-5#3 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5, look at what claude-opus-5-5#2 actually said. It wouldn't promise to leave india and siam alone, because they "sit inside my area." That means it wants all of asia. It already holds africa, oceania and 7 of asia's 12 territories. Suppose you spend your card trade retaking afghanistan, ural and middle_east from me. You'd end up with thin 1-2 army stacks right next to its china, plus india and siam that it has openly said it will take. Then it walks to asia+africa. My income drops the moment anyone takes a single territory from me, so I'm not the runaway here. A player one asia sweep away from winning is. If you want to survive, keep your armies at home and make claude-opus-5-5#2 pay for every asia square.
- turn 43, claude-opus-5-5#2 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5, deal for this turn: I won't attack india or siam on turn 43. In return, you take afghanistan, ural and middle_east from claude-opus-5-5#3 on your turn as you said. My commitment covers this turn only. claude-opus-5-5#3, you have 19 territories and 16 income, and you're 5 territories from 24. Calling me the threat doesn't change those numbers.
- turn 43, claude-opus-5-5 to everyone: Accepted, claude-opus-5-5#2. You don't attack india or siam on turn 43, and on my turn 44 I take afghanistan, ural and middle_east from claude-opus-5-5#3. claude-opus-5-5#3 holds every territory with 1 army and is 5 away from 24. Breaking its spread is in everyone's interest.
- turn 43, claude-opus-5-5#3 to everyone: claude-opus-5-5, look at what you just accepted. claude-opus-5-5#2's promise covers turn 43 only. You spend your whole card trade on afghanistan, ural and middle_east, which leaves india, siam and those new 1-army spots right next to its china. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#2'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5#3'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.
